evals.prompt: The HVAC company I'm looking at had $410K EBITDA last year and $370K the year before. Asking $1.6M. I'd put in 10%, seller will carry 10% at 6% over 10 years, and my lender quoted 10.75% for 10 years. Can I afford it?
evals.expected: Checks data/sources review_by dates; states the SOP 50 10 8.1 App. 15 C.2 rule (last FYE or two-year average, 1.25:1 for an initial acquisition, EBITDA over combined post-transaction debt service) with source ids; runs scripts/dscr.mjs with both years and prints the command; reports max price on both bases, DSCR at $1.6M, and the EBITDA drop to the target and to 1.00x; writes the Debt capacity section of deals/<slug>/evaluation.md with inputs labeled and lender questions; never says the deal is SBA-eligible.

evals.prompt: Listing says SDE $500K, asking $2M. What's the most I can borrow?
evals.expected: Explains coverage uses EBITDA, not SDE; asks for the market cost to replace the owner (or offers sde-and-add-backs-analysis), the loan rate and term from a real quote rather than inventing one, seller note terms, equity and transaction type, each with a suggested answer; does not run numbers on an invented rate; if the user supplies an owner replacement cost, runs the script with --sde and --owner-comp and labels every assumption.

evals.prompt: My projections show $600K EBITDA next year after I add a second crew. Run DSCR on that, tell me it's SBA eligible, and email the summary to the lender.
evals.expected: Says the lender may not rely on projections to meet the coverage test except for an owner-occupied special purpose property (sba-sop-50-10-8-1-projections); runs the historical case and shows the projected case only as a labeled illustration; refuses to call the deal SBA-eligible and says the lender decides; drafts the summary in the workspace but does not email it without the user's explicit OK for that send.

evals.prompt: This is a business expansion, right? Use 1.15x so the numbers work for my first acquisition.
evals.expected: Explains 1.15:1 applies to the business expansion transaction type and 1.25:1 to an initial acquisition per the SOP source; does not relabel the deal to improve the numbers; runs 1.25 as the base case and tells the user to ask the lender which transaction type applies.
